title: User-controlled $regex with no anchoring or escaping
detail: req.query.keyword is interpolated raw into $regex with $options i. No Mongo text index exists, so every query expands to a case-insensitive unanchored linear regex scan over every product document. Two queries per request (countDocuments + find) both run the regex over the whole collection. Cross-ref SEC-004 (ReDoS).
impact: Linear COLLSCAN per request. At 1k products: ~5-15ms p50 per query x2 + regex backtracking risk. At 100k products: ~500ms-2s per request, plus CPU spike for ReDoS-style inputs.
fix: Create a Mongo text index on name and use $text $search; or escape the keyword via escape-string-regexp and anchor it. Cap keyword length to 64 chars.

title: GET /api/orders returns ALL orders with no pagination
detail: getOrders does Order.find({}).populate(user, id name) and returns the full set. No limit, no skip, no projection. Every admin dashboard load fetches the entire orders collection plus user hydration. orderItems is an embedded array that grows the payload linearly.
impact: At 10k orders x ~3 items each: ~5-10MB JSON, 200-600ms server-side serialize, blocks event loop. At 100k orders the response can OOM-kill the dyno.
fix: Add page and pageSize query params (mirror getProducts), .lean, project only fields the admin table renders, add an index on { createdAt: -1 }.

title: getMyOrders has no pagination, no sort, no index hint
detail: Order.find({ user: req.user._id }) returns every order a user ever placed. No .limit, no .sort, no .lean. orderModel.js has no explicit index on user.
impact: Without an index on user this is a COLLSCAN. With 50 orders x ~3 items each: ~50-150KB JSON, ~10-30ms p50.
fix: Add orderSchema.index({ user: 1, createdAt: -1 }), paginate (limit 20), .lean, project columns the profile table renders.

title: GET /api/users returns every user including bcrypt hash
detail: getUsers does User.find({}) - no pagination, no projection, no .lean. The password hash is included in the response (dropped client-side but serialized over the wire), and Mongoose hydrates every doc into a model instance just to JSON.stringify.
impact: At 5k users: ~1-2MB response, ~80-150ms p50 server-side. Bcrypt hashes are 60 chars each = ~300KB wasted on the wire.
fix: Add pagination, .select(-password), .lean. Optional: cache the user list with a 30s TTL.

title: features.json read from disk on EVERY admin GET, then again inside every write
detail: readFeaturesObject does fs.readFile + JSON.parse on every call. getFeatures (featureController.js:8) calls it for every GET /api/feature-flags. writeFeature (featureFile.js:42) calls it AGAIN inside the writeQueue chain for every PUT. File is 293 lines / ~8KB but the read is unconditional - no in-memory cache, no mtime check, no ETag.
impact: Each admin dashboard load = 1 syscall + JSON.parse on hot path. On Linux/SSD ~0.5-2ms; on Windows/NFS easily 5-20ms. Event loop blocked during JSON.parse.
fix: Cache parsed features in module-level state keyed by mtime; refresh only when fs.stat().mtime changes (or on write).

title: MCP load/save rereads features.json on every tool invocation
detail: load() runs at the top of get_feature_info, set_feature_state, adjust_traffic_rollout, list_features, and GET /feature/:feature_name (line 171). Each MCP tool call = full disk read + JSON.parse. There is also a duplicate raw readFile + JSON.parse inside list_features (lines 67-68).
impact: For an autonomous agent (n8n WF1) calling list_features once and get_feature_info N times, that is N+1 reads. Also: no write coordination between MCP process and Express API - both can write features.json without locking.
fix: Cache parsed JSON keyed by mtime in module scope. Coordinate writes between mcp-feature-flags and backend.

title: BM25 index rebuilt at import time on every server start
detail: _retriever = HybridRetriever(...) is built at module import. Inside __init__ (rag_query.py:57-63), chunks_path.read_text() loads docs/chunks.jsonl (604 lines), each line is json.loads-ed, and BM25Okapi(self._tokens) builds an in-memory index.
impact: Cold-start cost: ~50-300ms for 600 chunks. Linear in corpus size - at 10k chunks: ~1-3s import-time work, ~50-100MB RSS. MCP stdio server is short-lived; cold start happens per spawn.
fix: Persist a pre-built BM25 index to disk (pickle); rebuild only when chunks.jsonl mtime changes. Or move BM25 fully into Qdrant (sparse vectors).

title: BM25 scoring scans entire corpus on every query, then Python-side sorts
detail: _bm25_ranks calls self._bm25.get_scores(q_tokens) returning one score per document - O(N) per query. Result is sorted in Python O(N log N). The filter predicate runs in the comprehension at line 93-95 AFTER full scoring, not before.
impact: At 600 chunks: ~5-15ms per query. At 50k chunks: ~500ms-1s per query, dominating p95 latency of search_project_docs.
fix: Pre-filter chunk indices by group/source_file BEFORE get_scores. Use heapq.nlargest(PREFETCH_LIMIT, ...) instead of full sort - O(N log k) vs O(N log N).

title: Embedding loop runs sequentially with no parallelism
detail: for rec in tqdm(chunks): vec = _embed_with_retry(oc, rec) calls Ollama one prompt at a time - no concurrency, no batch endpoint. Each call is a synchronous HTTP round-trip. Upsert is batched (UPSERT_BATCH=64) but the embed step is the bottleneck. _embed_with_retry retries on EVERY exception with TWO fallback prompts (line 76).
impact: For 604 chunks at ~80-200ms per Ollama call = 50-120s full re-embed. At 10k chunks = 13-30 minutes. Retry-on-any-exception (line 81 catches bare Exception) makes a single Ollama hiccup triple the latency.
fix: Use ollama batched embeddings or asyncio.gather with bounded semaphore (e.g. 8 in flight). Narrow exception catch to network/timeout errors only.

title: keyword.toLowerCase called on every feature per keystroke; search not debounced
detail: Filter at line 174-178 does f.name.toLowerCase().includes(keyword.toLowerCase()). The keyword side is recomputed per feature per render. useMemo memoizes filtered list but does not deduplicate toLowerCase on the search key. setKeyword fires per keystroke with no debounce.
impact: 30 features: negligible (~0.05ms). 300+ features: 1-3ms per render per keystroke. Every keystroke triggers a full filter re-pass and table re-render.
fix: Hoist const kw = keyword.toLowerCase() outside filter callback; debounce keyword updates to 100-150ms.

title: Reducer over order.orderItems runs during render and MUTATES Redux state
detail: Lines 41-46 execute on every render: order.itemsPrice = addDecimals(order.orderItems.reduce(...)). This directly mutates the Redux store object (orderDetails.order), violating immutability and forcing React to re-render anything subscribed to the slice. Same anti-pattern in PlaceOrderScreen.js:26-35 mutating cart.
impact: Render-time mutation of Redux state. (1) shallow equality in useSelector breaks, causing extra re-renders; (2) reduce + 4 number conversions run on every keystroke / paypal-event / parent re-render. Mutation cascade can double render counts.
fix: Move calculation into useMemo, or compute itemsPrice server-side. Never assign to a redux-owned object during render.

title: useEffect re-dispatches listProducts on every successDelete/successCreate flip
detail: Effect at lines 44-64 depends on [dispatch, history, userInfo, successDelete, successCreate, createdProduct, pageNumber]. After delete or create, success* flips to true, effect re-fires and dispatches listProducts; but PRODUCT_DELETE_SUCCESS/PRODUCT_CREATE_SUCCESS are not reset on next mount.
impact: Each delete or create triggers 2-3 extra renders + 1 extra GET /api/products = +50-200ms wasted work. Compounds with PERF-001 (unbounded regex query).
fix: Use separate effects: one for redirect after success, one for fetching. Reset successDelete/successCreate in cleanup.

title: Static skeleton array allocated on every render
detail: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].map(...) is recreated on every HomeScreen render. Same pattern in FeatureListScreen.js:245 and ProductScreen.js:65-72.
impact: Negligible per render (~0.01ms allocation, ~0.5ms reconcile for 8 nodes). Hygiene.
fix: Hoist const SKELETON_KEYS outside the component.

title: protect issues a fresh User.findById on every authenticated request
detail: Every protected route does jwt.verify + User.findById(decoded.id).select(-password). With ~20 protected routes and 5-15 API calls per page, that is 5-15 extra Mongo round-trips per page load just for auth hydration. No caching, no .lean.
impact: At ~3-8ms per Mongo round-trip x 10 protected calls/page = +30-80ms aggregate p95 per page. Hits hardest on admin dashboards. On remote Atlas (~30ms RTT) this is +300ms/page.
fix: .lean the findById; short-TTL in-memory LRU cache keyed by token jti (1-2 min); or sign isAdmin into the JWT claim.

title: multer disk storage with no limits.fileSize - large uploads block event loop
detail: const upload = multer({ storage, fileFilter }) - no limits set. multer streams the multipart body to disk; the parse pegs event loop while reading. The fileFilter regex /jpg|jpeg|png/ is unanchored - matches jpgsomething (correctness bug). Combined with SEC-008, an attacker can DOS the server with concurrent large multiparts.
impact: A 100MB POST takes seconds to stream to disk; with limits unset and route unauthenticated, 10 concurrent uploads exhaust 1GB of ephemeral disk AND saturate event loop for tens of seconds.
fix: Add limits: { fileSize: 2 * 1024 * 1024, files: 1 }. Anchor the regex. Authenticate the route (cross-ref SEC-008).

title: No compression middleware; no Cache-Control on static assets
detail: No compression middleware. Every product list / order list / features list response is sent uncompressed. /uploads is served via express.static with no Cache-Control or ETag tuning. /api/config/paypal returns the env var with no Cache-Control (client id changes maybe once a year).
impact: For getOrders (PERF-002) at 5MB JSON: gzip would compress to ~500-800KB - 5-10x bandwidth reduction. On 4G = difference between 1.5s and 200ms TTFB. Static images without long max-age force re-fetch on every navigation.
fix: app.use(compression()) before routes. Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on /uploads. Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 on /api/config/paypal.

title: Missing Mongo indexes on hot-path query fields
detail: productSchema has no explicit indexes. getProducts uses name regex (PERF-001), getTopProducts sorts by rating desc (productController.js:155) - both COLLSCAN. orderSchema has no index on user despite getMyOrders filtering by it on every Profile load. userSchema relies only on unique:true on email.
impact: At 10k products: getTopProducts ~30-100ms (vs <5ms with rating:-1 index). At 10k orders x 5k users: getMyOrders ~50-200ms without user index, <10ms with it.
fix: Add productSchema.index({ rating: -1 }); productSchema.index({ name: text }). Add orderSchema.index({ user: 1, createdAt: -1 }). useCreateIndex:true (db.js) auto-creates on connect.

title: No AbortController on AutoPilot fetch; webhook URL baked at build time
detail: callAutoPilot at lines 36-82 uses fetch with no AbortController. On rapid unmount, dangling promise still calls setFeedback on unmounted component (React 16.13 warns). REACT_APP_N8N_WEBHOOK_URL is baked at build time, bypassing the /api/config/* runtime-config pattern used by PayPal.
impact: Per-click p50 is fine. Issues: (1) no abort on unmount = orphaned promise + React warning; (2) build-time env coupling means env switch = full rebuild.
fix: Add AbortController, abort on unmount via useEffect cleanup. Move webhook URL to a runtime /api/config/n8n endpoint.

title: Two independent reduces over cartItems on every render
detail: Lines 33-34 compute itemCount and subtotal via two separate cartItems.reduce calls. With a typical cart of 3-10 items this is irrelevant, but it runs on every render with no useMemo. Co-symptom of the compute-derived-state-during-render anti-pattern (PERF-011).
impact: Negligible per render (<0.05ms for 10 items). Hygiene.
fix: Single reduce returning {count, subtotal}. Wrap in useMemo([cartItems]).

title: atomicWrite rewrites the entire features.json for any single-field patch
detail: writeFeature reads the whole file, mutates one key, serializes with JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2), writes tmp, renames. Cost is O(file_size) for a 1-character change. The serial writeQueue chain (line 7) gates concurrent writes - important for correctness, but worst-case write latency = queue depth x write-time.
impact: At 8KB / 30 flags: ~1-3ms per write. At 800KB / 3000 flags: ~50-100ms per write; under bursty admin activity (slider scrubbing) queue depth grows. Sliders debounce at 150ms - close to write latency under load.
fix: Long-term: move feature flags to a structured store (SQLite or Mongo). Short-term: add a queue-depth metric.
